title: Other Node core modules
lede: The smaller Node built-ins, grouped here rather than each given a full page. The recurring divergence is that anything nominally async is blocking under the hood — net/tls/dns/dgram fold their file descriptors into one select() loop, so a slow peer stalls it and connect/handshake failures throw a catchable Error rather than emitting an async 'error' event. Messages across process and channel boundaries (cluster, diagnostics_channel) are strings, the http/https clients are GET-only over libcurl, and vm stays out of scope behind the same blocker as bare eval().

entries.name: querystring (.parse, .stringify)
entries.signature: querystring.parse(str: string): Map<string,string>; querystring.stringify(m: Map<string,string>): string
entries.description: The legacy "a=b&c=d" parse/stringify pair, largely superseded by URLSearchParams but a natural companion when a request handler already holds a Map<string,string>. A Map goes in and comes out — the same shape req.query and URLSearchParams already use. .parse does not strip a leading '?' (matching real Node, and distinct from new URLSearchParams(str), which does).

params.name: str / m
params.desc: A raw query tail to parse, or a Map to serialize.

returns.desc: The parsed map, or the serialized query string.

entries.snippet:
const parsed = querystring.parse("name=Ada&topic=compilers%20and%20types")
console.log(parsed.get("topic"))  // compilers and types

entries.name: assert (.ok, bare assert(cond, msg?), .equal/.strictEqual, .notEqual/.notStrictEqual, .deepEqual/.deepStrictEqual (+not*), .fail, .throws, .match/.doesNotMatch)
entries.signature: assert(cond: boolean, msg?: string): void; assert.strictEqual(a, b); assert.deepStrictEqual(a, b); assert.throws(fn)
entries.description: Node's real assertion library — distinct from console.assert, which logs and continues. A failure throws a catchable AssertionError (kind-tagged as a base Error, since this compiler's fixed error-kind enum has no dedicated slot), the shape scripts and tests actually use.
differences: `equal`/`strictEqual` and `deepEqual`/`deepStrictEqual` (and their `not*` counterparts) are aliases of each other — this compiler's `==` has no implicit coercion to distinguish them
`deepStrictEqual` covers scalars, strings, arrays, and objects (recursively, incl. nested); Map/Set/class instances, nullable-scalar members, and TypedArrays are a clean compile error (V1)
`.match`/`.doesNotMatch`'s regexp argument must be statically a RegExp
`.throws` only checks that *something* was thrown, not the thrown value's type/message

entries.name: test / node:test (the **runner**: test/it, describe/suite, TestContext t.test/t.after/t.skip/t.todo/t.diagnostic, hooks before/after/beforeEach/afterEach — plus the native helpers mustCall/mustCallAtLeast/mustNotCall/skip/expectsError + env probes)
entries.statusRow: test / node:test (the **runner**: test/it, describe/suite, TestContext t.test/t.after/t.skip/t.todo/t.diagnostic, hooks before/after/beforeEach/afterEach — plus the native helpers mustCall/mustCallAtLeast/mustNotCall/skip/expectsError + env probes)
entries.signature: import { test, describe, mustCall } from 'test'; test(name, fn); mustCall(fn, n=1)
entries.description: The node:test runner plus the native helpers. mustCall is a first-class builtin (not Node's internal ../common): it wraps fn so its invocation count is verified at process exit via the existing exit sink — an unmet or exceeded count prints a diagnostic and exits non-zero, giving examples and tests real async assertions instead of console.log.
differences: Runner: **run-at-registration** (top-level code after a `test()` runs after it here, before it in Node); `beforeEach`/`afterEach` are single slots (last wins) and also fire for subtests; no `mock.*`, `t.plan`, `run()`, concurrency, or snapshots

`mustCall` supports callbacks of **0–3 simple (scalar/pointer) parameters** — a rest param, >3 args, or an array/nullable-scalar param is a clean compile error (the counting trampoline is signature-parametric)
`mustNotCall()` returns a `() => void`; using it where a non-zero-arity callback is expected is a type mismatch
`mustSucceed` is count-only (the "err is falsy" check is deferred); `expectWarning` runs the thunk but doesn't capture warnings

entries.name: util (.inspect, .format)
entries.description: .inspect reuses the same value formatter as console.log (strings single-quoted, ClassName { … }, arrays, 10n). .format handles %s/%d/%i/%f/%j/%o/%O/%%, appends excess args space-separated, and leaves unrecognized specifiers literal — matching Node.
differences: No `.promisify` — the callback builtins (`zlib.gzip`, `child_process.exec`) are name-dispatched calls, not first-class function values to wrap; importing `promisify` fails cleanly
`.format` requires a string-**literal** format (compile-time walk); a runtime format string is a compile error
`.inspect`'s options object is accepted but ignored (no `depth`/`colors`)

entries.name: net (TCP server: net.createServer, server.listen/address()/on('connection'|'listening')/close; TCP client: net.connect/createConnection (positional or { port, host }); connection socket .on('data'|'end')/.write/.end/.address()/.destroy()/.setNoDelay()/.setKeepAlive(); net.isIP/isIPv4/isIPv6)
entries.statusRow: net (TCP server: net.createServer, server.listen/address()/on('connection'|'listening')/close; TCP client: net.connect/createConnection (positional or { port, host }); connection socket .on('data'|'end')/.write/.end/.address()/.destroy()/.setNoDelay()/.setKeepAlive(); net.isIP/isIPv4/isIPv6)
entries.description: TCP server and client. The accept loop and per-connection read pipes fold into the same select() event loop as child_process; a client socket reuses the same machinery once connected. 'data' delivers a Buffer; .write/.end take a string/Buffer/ArrayBuffer/DataView. address() reads the real bound address+port via getsockname+inet_ntop, making the listen(0) ephemeral-port idiom usable; net.isIP parses via inet_pton (0/4/6).
differences: `net.connect` uses a **blocking** `connect()` — a slow/unreachable host blocks the event loop until the OS connect timeout; a connect failure **throws** a catchable `Error` rather than emitting an async `'error'` event

Server binds IPv4 `0.0.0.0` only (no `host`/`path`/options object on `listen`); `.address()` reports the **real** bound address/port via `getsockname` (`{ family: "IPv4", address, port }`) — for a server that's `0.0.0.0`, for a connected socket its real local IP (e.g. `127.0.0.1`). Because the bind is IPv4-native, an accepted socket reports `127.0.0.1` where Node's dual-stack default reports `::ffff:127.0.0.1`, and the server reports `IPv4`/`0.0.0.0` not `IPv6`/`::`
`net.connect` accepts every positional arity (`(port)`, `(port, cb)`, `(port, host[, cb])`) and `{ port, host }` (host defaults to `localhost`); the IPC `{ path }` form is TCP-only-unsupported
`on('listening')` fires when the server binds (registered before or after `listen()`); no `'error'`/`'close'`/`'connect'` events on server or socket yet

`socket.setNoDelay`/`setKeepAlive` are real `setsockopt` calls; `setEncoding`/`ref`/`unref`/`pause`/`resume`/`setTimeout` are **accepted but no-ops** (the blocking read model has no separately-schedulable flow or idle timer, and a socket's chunk type already follows the listener's declared parameter type)
No back-pressure: `.write` never returns `false` and there's no `'drain'` event
Listeners must be arrow/function-expression literals
`net.Server`/`net.Socket` are not exposed as constructible classes

entries.name: dgram (UDP sockets: createSocket('udp4'), bind, address(), on('message'), send, close)
entries.statusRow: dgram (UDP sockets: createSocket('udp4'), bind, address(), on('message'), send, close)
entries.description: UDP sockets. Each socket's fd folds into the same select() event loop as net/child_process. 'message' fires with a Buffer and an rinfo { address, port }; send(msg, port, host) resolves host (name or IP) via the dns helper. msg/send payloads take a string/Buffer/ArrayBuffer/DataView.
differences: `udp4` only — no `udp6`
No `'listening'`/`'error'` events, options object, or multicast
Message listeners must be arrow/function-expression literals
`socket.send(msg, port, host)` positional form only — no `(msg, offset, length, port, address, cb)` form; no `.address()`/`.setBroadcast()`/`.setTTL()`/membership methods

entries.name: tls (TLS-wrapped sockets)
entries.signature: tls.connect(port, host[, {rejectUnauthorized}][, onSecureConnect]); tls.createServer({ cert, key }, connectionListener)
entries.description: Client tls.connect (cert verification + SNI on by default) and server tls.createServer({ cert, key }) both return net-shaped handles (an SSL* in the socket), so .on('data')/.write()/.end()/.on('connection') reuse the net machinery, routing through SSL_read/SSL_write. A handshake or verify failure throws a catchable Error.
differences: **Blocking** TCP connect + TLS handshake on both sides (a slow peer stalls the loop), the same simplification `net.connect` makes
OpenSSL-only (libssl) — a `-crypto=commoncrypto` build using `tls` is a clean compile error (Mac's CommonCrypto has no TLS API)

Client options `{ rejectUnauthorized }` only (SNI = the host; no client-cert / ALPN / `servername` override); server `{ cert, key }` are PEM **strings** only (one cert per server, no chain/passphrase, no `requestCert`); the options may be an object literal or a bound object value

entries.name: dns (dns.lookup, dns.resolve4/resolve, dns.promises.lookup)
entries.signature: dns.lookup(host, cb); dns.resolve4(host, cb); await dns.promises.lookup(host)
entries.description: getaddrinfo(3)-backed name resolution. lookup returns one dotted-quad, resolve4 all A records as a string[], promises.lookup a Promise<{address, family}>.
differences: `dns.resolve4`/`resolve` use `getaddrinfo` (the OS resolver), not real DNS `A` queries — no `resolve6`/`resolveMx`/`resolveTxt`/`reverse`
IPv4 (`AF_INET`) only; `family` is always 4
The callback forms fire synchronously, not on a later event-loop tick
Failure passes a generic `Error` (`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`), not a `code`-tagged Node error

entries.name: zlib (gzip/gunzip, deflate/inflate, deflateRaw/inflateRaw, unzip, each *Sync + (err, result) callback)
entries.statusRow: zlib (gzip/gunzip, deflate/inflate, deflateRaw/inflateRaw, unzip, each *Sync + (err, result) callback)
entries.signature: zlib.gzipSync(input): Buffer; zlib.gunzipSync(buf): Buffer; zlib.gzip(input, (err, out) => …)
entries.description: One-shot compression over the same libz backend as CompressionStream, driven by a shared @__kml_zlib_oneshot helper. Input may be a Buffer/TypedArray, ArrayBuffer, DataView, or string (UTF-8); output is always a Buffer.

params.name: input
params.desc: The data to compress or decompress.

differences: The callback form fires synchronously, not deferred to the next event-loop tick
No Brotli (`brotliCompress*`) — it would pull in `-lbrotli`, a new system dependency this binding deliberately avoids
No class/stream forms (`createGzip()`, `zlib.Gzip`, …) — the WHATWG `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream` cover the streaming case
`{ level }` is the only supported option and must be a compile-time constant

entries.name: vm (vm.Script, sandboxed eval-like execution)
entries.description: Not implemented. vm hits the same fundamental blocker as bare eval() — there is no embedded engine to run source assembled at runtime. An opt-in embedded-engine path is scoped but not started.

entries.name: diagnostics_channel (channel/subscribe/unsubscribe/hasSubscribers, Channel .publish/.hasSubscribers/.name)
entries.description: Name-keyed pub/sub: channel/subscribe/unsubscribe/hasSubscribers, with a Channel handle exposing .publish/.hasSubscribers/.name. Subscribers may be 0/1/2-arity, and unsubscribe is by pointer identity.

returns.desc: A channel handle, subscription result, or nothing.

differences: Messages are **strings** (serialize with `JSON.stringify`) — a typed subset can't hand arbitrary object shapes to unknown subscribers
Subscriber params must be string-typed (an untyped pre-wrapped subscriber is a clean rejection, never silent reinterpretation)
`tracingChannel` and the store bindings (`bindStore`/`runStores`) are clean rejections; a Channel handle isn't module-global-promotable (capture it in a closure, not a named top-level function)

entries.name: http client (http.get/http.request)
entries.signature: http.get(url, res => …); const req = http.request(opts); req.end()
entries.description: A libcurl-backed HTTP client with async event-loop delivery and contextually-typed callbacks (including test wrappers). Both http.get and http.request return a ClientRequest handle.

returns.desc: A request handle; the response arrives via callback.

differences: GET only (no request bodies/method override — `req.end(body)` is a clean rejection); response surface is `res.statusCode`/`res.on('data'/'end')`/`res.resume()`/`setEncoding`

Both calls return a ClientRequest handle: `request()` sends nothing until `.end()`; `.abort()`/`.destroy()` cancel only a not-yet-fired request (an in-flight transfer isn't torn down); `.on('error')` is accepted but never fired — transport failures throw instead

`new http.Agent(options)`/`new https.Agent(options)` construct an inert token: recognized pool options are validated but configure nothing (one connection per request), `.destroy()` is a no-op, and `.sockets`/`.requests` reject cleanly
Options objects (literal **or variable-bound**) support `{ port, path, host/hostname, agent }`; `headers`/`method` are clean rejections
`agent` is accepted and ignored — this client opens one connection per request (Node's own `agent: false` behavior); `new http.Agent(...)` itself is not implemented, and no pooling ever happens

entries.name: https (client: https.get/https.request)
entries.signature: https.get(url, res => …); const req = https.request(opts); req.end()
entries.description: get/request ride the same libcurl backend as the http client, so the TLS handshake and certificate verification come from the URL scheme — no https-specific machinery. Verified against a live TLS host on Mac.

returns.desc: A request handle; the response arrives via callback.

differences: **Client only** — `https.createServer` is a clean rejection (the HTTP accept loop is not TLS-wrapped; use `tls.createServer` for a raw TLS socket server, or terminate TLS in front of `http.createServer`)
Same V1 client surface and caveats as `http.get`/`request`

entries.name: stream/web (re-exports: ReadableStream/WritableStream/TransformStream/CompressionStream/DecompressionStream)
entries.description: The names bind as identity to the ambient WHATWG constructors that already exist — importing them from stream/web is interchangeable with using the globals. The queuing-strategy classes are not exported.

returns.desc: The same ambient constructors as the globals.

entries.name: cluster (fork, worker messaging, isPrimary/isWorker/workerId, Worker.id/.process)
entries.description: Unifies with http.listen({ workers: N })'s worker-id global — the primary stays in the event loop while workers live (via their IPC handles), then blocks in waitpid as the backstop. Workers carry the fork IPC channel: worker.send/.on('message'/'online'/'exit'/'close'/'error')/.disconnect()/.kill()/.destroy()/.process.pid; in-worker process.send/process.on('message').
differences: Messages are strings; one listener per event; `'online'` fires from a queued microtask (the worker is exec'd by then), not a wire handshake
No `cluster.on(...)` (cluster-level events), `cluster.workers` map, `cluster.disconnect()`, `setupPrimary()`(`setupMaster`)/`settings`
Workers each bind the port via `SO_REUSEPORT`; on Linux the kernel load-balances accepts across them, on Darwin the distribution is uneven (often one worker) — correctness holds, balancing differs
Can't be combined with Worker threads (same restriction as `http.listen({workers})`)

entries.name: http2 **module** (http2.createServer/connect, Http2Session/Http2Stream)
entries.description: The explicit http2 module, over the same nghttp2 h2c driver that http.listen already rides transparently. Server-side serves h2c (and still answers 1.1, a superset of Node); the client opens an h2c session and submits body-less requests.
differences: **Server-side Stages 1–2**: `http2.createServer` on the http server handle, serving **h2c** (it also still answers 1.1, a superset of Node); compat `.on('request', (req, res))` **and** the core streams API — `.on('stream', (stream, headers))` with pseudo-headers on the map, `stream.respond({ ':status', … })` incl. response headers, `.end`/`.write`, request body via `.on('data'|'end')` (one synchronous chunk)
`stream.close()`/`setEncoding`/`resume`/`pause` are accepted no-ops; responses are written when the handler returns (no mid-stream RST/flow control)

**Client (Stage 3)**: `http2.connect("http://…")` (h2c only — a TLS authority throws) → session `.request({ ':path', ':method', headers… })` → stream `.on('response'|'data'|'end')`; requests are **body-less** (END_STREAM at submit — `req.write`/`end(body)` are clean rejections); response `':status'` arrives as a *string* in the headers map (Node types it as a number); session/stream `'error'`/`'close'` listeners are accepted no-ops

**Stage 4**: `http2.constants` (compile-time namespace — header/method names, RFC 7540 error codes; unknown members reject cleanly) and `getDefaultSettings`/`getPackedSettings`/`getUnpackedSettings` (nghttp2 wire format; the invalid-value RangeError taxonomy is not modeled)
`createSecureServer` (needs a TLS server mode) and request bodies remain **clean rejections**
Sessions, streams, server/client push, settings frames, and the whole explicit-API surface are unimplemented — staged over the existing nghttp2 h2c driver; client-mode nghttp2 is the main new work
